articles.summary_snippet: A trilateral gathering is good news for China and Russia, but bad for the US – and its traditional allies “Historic” is a neutral descriptor, not a favourable one. Things can be unprecedented for good reason. Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China on Thursday will be the first time that the leaders of the US, China and Russia have gathered for talks as a trio. The trilateral on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is striking, but it is not an achievement. The lack of a clear agenda is telling: the spectacle really is the substance. Mr Trump sees international affairs in terms of spheres of influence. This meeting reinforces the obvious conclusion for the rest of the world – that they don’t get to sit at the table, only to be on the plate. Mr Xi promotes the notion of a multipolar world. articles.title: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
articles.summary_snippet: With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south. Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions. Continue reading...

Nobody in her family served, but my paternal grandfather fought in the Pacific in the second world war, and she was always grateful to hear his stories, even the repeats. It’s one of the things she gave me that I held on to, even in my worst years. The anger I’ve carried about the unjust wars of my lifetime – Afghanistan, Iraq and now Iran – never targeted the people sent to fight them. Continue reading...

For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge. India has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. articles.summary_snippet: NWS issues advisories for long stretches of the northern California coast, warning that waves can quickly overpower anyone nearby The massive, 50-ft swells along California’s coast this weekend foretold an intense week of towering waves to come. Officials from the National Weather Service (NWS) had issued advisories for long stretches of the California coast, warning people that erratic and unpredictable waves could quickly overpower anyone nearby. The highest waves – which reached 50ft to 60ft (15.24 to 18.29 meters) – cracked along the popular Mavericks surf spot in San Mateo county, south of San Francisco. Continue reading...
